_what: Ten built Nepali run-of-river plants used to validate Ghatta against reality. Coordinates and specifications were researched independently of the app — nothing here was chosen to make the comparison look good, and the derivations are stated so they can be re-checked.
_coordinateNote: intake/powerhouse are [lat, lon]. 'derived' means the point was placed on the OSM-mapped stream at the published waterway length upstream of the powerhouse — the DEM was never consulted, so the head comparison stays independent. 'approx' means village-level accuracy.
_excluded: Jhimruk and Andhikhola divert water through a ridge into a different valley; Ghatta deliberately models same-valley schemes only, so they cannot be run. Kulekhani is storage, not run-of-river.

plants.name: Upper Tamakoshi
plants.intakeSource: OSM: 'Upper Tamakoshi Headworks Diversion Dam' (way centre)
plants.note: Nepal's largest plant. Peaking run-of-river with a 22 m dam. Most of its catchment lies north of the border on the Tibetan plateau, where every global flow product this app can reach runs low together and HYDEST — fitted to Nepali catchments — is out of its domain. The feasibility study stood on years of site gauging; nothing less answers here.

plants.name: Kali Gandaki A
plants.powerhouseSource: Wikipedia infobox: powerhouse at Beltari; matches OSM plant polygon
plants.note: 44 m high dam raises the intake level well above the riverbed; Ghatta models a low weir, so it should under-read the head here by roughly the dam height.

plants.name: Middle Marsyangdi
plants.note: Peaking run-of-river with five hours of daily pondage.

plants.name: Marsyangdi
plants.intakeSource: Wikipedia station coordinate (dam upstream of Aanbu Khaireni)
plants.powerhouseSource: OSM: 'Marsyangdi Hydro Power' plant polygon at Aanbukhaireni
plants.note: Design flow is 3 turbines at 30.5 m³/s each. Peaking plant: its dam ponds the river well above the bed, and Ghatta models a low weir reading the riverbed — so an under-read head here is the model being honest about what it measures, not a terrain error.

plants.name: Khimti I
plants.intakeSource: derived: OSM-mapped Khimti Khola walked 9.3 km (published headrace + penstock) upstream of the Tamakoshi confluence
plants.powerhouseSource: downstream end of the OSM-mapped Khimti Khola (Kirne, at the Tamakoshi confluence); Wikipedia's 27.474, 86.101 corroborates
plants.note: Intake at el. 1270 m, tailrace to the Tamakoshi at el. 586 m — the published figures the head is checked against.

plants.name: Upper Marsyangdi A
plants.powerhouseSource: OSM: 'Upper Marsyangdi A Hydroelectric Station' plant polygon at Bhulbhule
plants.note: Design discharge and head are not published where they could be verified, so only capacity and energy are compared.

plants.name: Upper Bhote Koshi
plants.intakeSource: Global Energy Observatory: side intake ~500 m below the Jung Khola confluence near Tatopani
plants.note: Rebuilt after the 2015 earthquake and 2016 GLOF — the river that shows why hazard layers matter. The Bhote Koshi drains Tibet: the numbers land here, but nothing local can corroborate the global models on this river, so treat the agreement as luck to be verified, not a property to rely on.

plants.name: Mistri Khola
plants.intakeSource: approx: ~4 km up the Mistri Khola from the powerhouse per published tunnel (2.29 km) + penstock (1.42 km); the stream is unnamed in OSM so this is village-level accuracy
plants.powerhouseSource: OSM: 'Mistri Khola Powerhouse' (left bank of the Kali Gandaki below the confluence)
plants.note: High-head Pelton plant under the Nilgiri massif.

plants.name: Chameliya
plants.note: Far-western Nepal — the test that the data holds outside the famous central basins. Six-hour peaking: the dam ponds the river above the bed Ghatta reads, and pondage lets the design flow exceed what a pure run-of-river Q40 would be.

plants.name: Chilime
plants.intakeSource: derived: upstream end of the OSM-mapped Chilime Khola at Chilime village, 4.2 km along the stream from the powerhouse — matches the published 'about 4.5 km'
plants.powerhouseSource: Wikipedia plant coordinate (underground powerhouse above Syafrubesi)
plants.note: The plant Nepali engineers built themselves — the reason this tool exists.
